description.value:
Given a long rest, you assemble a set of malleable, portable fortifications that travel with you wherever you go. Only you can direct the structure — remotely if you're carrying a tech focus, or otherwise only while it's within 5 feet of you.

Its armor class equals your tech save DC, and it has hit points equal to five times your engineer level. If reduced to 0 hit points it collapses and can't be used again until you spend an hour repairing it (which can happen during a short or long rest). The mending tech power restores missing hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier (at least one), though it can never repair the structure above half its maximum this way; completing a short rest instead restores it to half its maximum, and a long rest restores it fully.

The structure has two states. Dismantled, it moves at your speed, hovers 5 feet above the ground, and occupies a 5-foot cube weighing 500 pounds — growing to a 10-foot cube and 1,000 pounds at 11th level, and a 15-foot cube and 2,000 pounds at 17th level. Deployed, its speed is 0 and its footprint depends on which structure you chose.

As an action, you can deploy the structure remotely into a space you can see within 30 feet (60 feet at 11th level, 120 feet at 17th level) that has room for it. Automatic dismantling takes 1 minute and can be started on your turn with no action required.

You can deploy your choice of the structures below a combined four times, gaining more uses at higher levels per the engineer table's Modification Slots column. Each use beyond your proficiency bonus reduces your tech point maximum by 1 until you complete a long rest, and all uses return after a long rest.

Bridge. A span up to 30 feet long, 10 feet wide, and 3 feet thick extends from your deployment point in a direction you choose, retracting back to that point when dismantled. Both ends must rest on solid support. It can bear up to 1,000 pounds; any greater weight instantly drops it to 0 hit points, destroying it. A creature standing on it when it's destroyed or dismantled must succeed on a Dexterity save against your tech save DC to reach stable footing or keep its grip as the bridge retracts, or fall on a failure. At 11th level, the bridge can reach 45 feet long and 15 feet wide and bear up to 2,000 pounds; at 17th level, 60 feet long, 20 feet wide, and 4,000 pounds.

Cage. You wall off a cube up to 10 feet on a side with opaque, 2-foot-thick barriers on every side but the ground; you decide whether it holds a bright light source or sits in total darkness, though air, water, and sound still pass through. Deploying it around an unwilling Medium or smaller creature forces that creature to succeed on a Dexterity save against your tech save DC to dash to the nearest open space outside the cage, or be trapped inside on a failure. At 11th level, the cage can reach 15 feet on a side and trap Large or smaller creatures; at 17th level, 20 feet on a side and Huge or smaller creatures.

Shelter. You raise a building up to 15 feet long, 10 feet wide, and 10 feet tall with one-foot-thick walls, roof, and floor, and a single door where you choose. It regulates temperature and light and shrugs off harsh wind, rain, and snow, shielding anyone inside from hazardous conditions like extreme heat or cold outside — though it supplies no extra breathable air if the environment itself is unbreathable. It comfortably houses 5 Medium creatures (or 2 Small creatures per Medium slot, or 2 Tiny per Small slot). At 11th level it grows to 30 feet by 15 feet by 15 feet and houses 10 Medium creatures under the same scaling, and anyone completing a long rest inside recovers all spent Hit Dice rather than half. At 17th level it grows to 45 feet by 20 feet by 20 feet and houses 10 Large creatures under the same scaling, and a long rest taken inside reduces exhaustion by 2 levels instead of 1.

Tower. A platform 5 feet square rises on a column up to 30 feet tall, complete with a ladder to the top; a creature standing where the tower rises must succeed on a Dexterity save (or choose to fail it) or be carried upward with the platform. At 11th level the platform grows to 5 by 10 feet and the column to 40 feet; at 17th level the platform becomes a 10-foot square, the column reaches 50 feet, and creatures atop it gain advantage on sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks.

Wall. You raise a straight wall up to 30 feet long, 10 feet high, and 3 feet thick — or a ring up to 10 feet across at the same height and thickness — with ramparts wide enough for Medium or smaller creatures, granting them one-quarter cover, plus a ladder on the side of your choice. You decide whether it has any see-through openings. A creature without a climbing speed needs a successful Strength (Athletics) check against your tech save DC, once per turn, to scale it. At 11th level the wall can reach 45 feet long and 15 feet high (or a 15-foot ring at that height) and its ramparts grant half cover; at 17th level, 60 feet long and 20 feet high (or a 20-foot ring at that height), granting three-quarters cover.
